# Utricularia × neglecta Lehm.

First published in Nov. Stirp. Pug. 1: 38 (1828)

This hybrid is accepted

The native range of this hybrid is Old World. It is a hydrosubshrub and grows primarily in the temperate biome. The hybrid formula is U. tenuicaulis × U. vulgaris.

### According to Angiosperm Extinction Risk Predictions v1

Extinction risk predictions for the world's flowering plants to support their conservation (2024). Bachman, S.P., Brown, M.J.M., Leão, T.C.C., Lughadha, E.N., Walker, B.E. https://nph.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/nph.19592

### According to Flora Zambesiaca under the synonym Littonia modesta

J. R. Timberlake, E. S. Martins (2009). Flora Zambesiaca, Vol 12 (part 2). Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

Type
    Type South Africa, Durban (Port Natal), x.1883, anderson s.n. (K holotype).
Morphology General Habit
    Perennial herb to 2 m
Vegetative Multiplication Corms
    Corm 5–6  c.2 cm, oblong
Morphology Stem
    Stem scandent, 60–200 cm high, the basal 18 cm lacking leaf
Morphology Leaves
    Leaves very numerous, set close together in whorls of 3–4, growing smaller and narrower towards stem apex, variable in width even on same plant, 10–17 0.5–3.5 cm, lanceolate or linear-lanceolate, tip drawn out into tendril c.2 cm long (included in leaf length)
Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers
    Flowers axillary, bright yellow or orange
Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Pedicel
    Pedicel 2–5.5 cm, bent at apex so flowers are nodding
Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Calyx
    Sepals and petals lanceolate, acute, united for 2–4 mm at base, 17–40 4–10 mm
Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Androecium Stamens Filaments
    Filaments c.7 mm long; anther c.8 mm long
Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Gynoecium Ovary
    Ovary 8–10 × 3 mm (possibly partly developed); style 4 mm long with 3 recurved branch 2–3 mm long.
Distribution
    Zimbabwe, Mozambique. Also in South Africa and Swaziland.
Ecology
    Woodland; 800–1500 m.
Conservation
    Conservation notes Widespread and not threatened globally, but within the Flora area likely to be Vulnerable.
[FZ]
